{{Quote|There is a purity to his loathing for the universe that is quite spiritually advanced.|[[Kardue'sai'Malloc/Legends|Kardue'sai'Malloc]]|<ref name="Devaronian's Tale">{{StoryCite|story=Empire Blues: The Devaronian's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref>}}
'''Wuher''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] who worked as a [[Bartender/Legends|bartender]] in [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. Wuher lived on Tatooine all of his life. His original training in the field came from a correspondence school.<ref name="Card-SWGTCG-Wuher">{{SWGTCG|set=Squadrons Over Corellia|cardname=Wuher}}</ref>

==Biography==

=== Early life ===
{{Quote|Bartenders in these sorts of places, frequented by different and unique biochemistries, were more xenoalchemists than simple pourers of drinks.|Wuher|<ref name="The Bartender's Tale" />}}
[[File:Wuherkid1.jpg|thumb|left|150px|A young Wuher.]]
As a child, Wuher lead a harsh life as an abandoned orphan living in Mos Eisley. As he grew he began to tinker with his chemistry kit, and developed a taste for interesting drinks which eventually lead him to bartending correspondence school. He was rejected by most people, and in [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]] experienced a horrific speeder crash while being driven through the streets of [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]] by a presumed [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]]. The man was abruptly assassinated in cold blood by [[Aurra Sing/Legends|Aurra Sing]] and then shapeshifted back into his original [[Shi'ido]] form. Sing then nonchalantly told a cowering Wuher that the world was tough, and that he should get used to it.<ref name="The Bounty Hunters: Aurra Sing">''[[The Bounty Hunters: Aurra Sing]]''</ref> Wuher's childhood gave rise to his overly gruff, sour attitude.

Later in life, Wuher was one of two bartenders at [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]]. The other bartender that he shared the role with was [[Ackmena/Legends|Ackmena]], a [[Gender/Legends|female]] Human. It was here that he developed a dislike toward [[Droid/Legends|droids]] and gained a certain satisfaction from removing them from the cantina. He claimed this was mainly due to the fact that they took up space in the cantina and did not require refreshment, but in fact he admitted only to himself, that droids were the only creatures he felt truly comfortable removing because he knew he could offend no one by asking.<ref name="The Bartender's Tale" /> At some point his [[EPT-212]] [[Droid detector/Legends|droid detector]] was stolen by a [[Jawa/Legends|Jawa]] trader named [[Dathcha/Legends|Dathcha]]. Wuher had hired a [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] to recover the detector, and when it was brought back, he promised the spacer an unlimited amount of free drinks in the cantina.<ref>{{SWGTCG|set=The Shadow Syndicate|scenario=Utinni! promotional scenario}}</ref>

As bartenders and bioalchemists went, Wuher was a genius. In a profession of serving drinks to an array of differing creatures and their biochemistry, simple humans were often distrusted with the ability to serve drinks safely. Despite this his knowledge of chemicals was exceptional, particularly when it applied to what substances are toxic, or merely intoxicating, to alien species. He was an expert at mixing the proper substances together to provide the most pleasant neurochemical reactions in his patrons. His most popular drinks were [[Blue milk/Legends|Blue milk]], [[Juri juice/Legends|Juri juice]], and [[Sarlacc kicker]], and he even invented a drink of his own called the [[Frosty Sulphate]].

Despite his personality, Wuher fostered a dream beneath his grizzly shell. He longed to make a signature drink that would earn him fame and wealth from [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]]. Working in the cantina's basement with an elaborate chemistry kit, Wuher worked daily, mixing all of Jabba's favorite drinks in perfect portions in an attempt to produce an elixir, a perfect [[Liqueur/Legends|liqueur]] suited exactly to the taste buds of [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]]. He imagined that one day the wealth this drink would provide would allow him to leave the detestable planet of [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="The Bartender's Tale" />

=== Galactic Civil War ===
[[File:Wuher_-_SWGTCg.jpg|thumb|Wuher, working in his cantina.]]
On the fateful day that [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] met [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] a [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], he told Luke to take two droids, [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], outside before he served him a glass of [[Water/Legends|water]], as per his policy. The fight between [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Cornelius Evazan/Legends|Cornelius Evazan]], [[Ponda Baba/Legends|Ponda Baba]], Luke Skywalker, and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] happened in front of his eyes. He also served the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Greedo/Legends|Greedo]], and eventually witnessed Han Solo killing Greedo on that very same day. Before these events, Wuher had been working below the cantina on Jabba's perfect drink. Wuher knew he had almost perfected the beverage, but it was slightly lacking. Relying on his exceptional sense of smell, he realized the pheromones Greedo exuded were the final flavor the drink required. Employing his newly found droid [[C2-R4]], he obtained Greedo's corpse and had C2-R4 brew Greedo into the liqueur. Upon tasting, Wuher believed he had finally created Jabba's perfect drink and at the same time, discovered a new-found sense of appreciation for droids.<ref name="The Bartender's Tale" />

The next day, he was called on by Mos Eisley police investigating the death of [[Feltipern Trevagg/Legends|Feltipern Trevagg]]. He informed them that [[H'nemthe (species)/Legends|H'nemthe]] females ritually disembowel their husbands on the wedding night.<ref name="Lovers">{{StoryCite|story=Nightlily: The Lovers' Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref>

Sometime later, Wuher found himself in the middle of firefight within his own cantina, when [[Thuku]] and a group of his thugs attacked a Rebel operative during a meeting.<ref>{{SWGTCG|set=Galactic Hunters|scenario=Light Side scenario campaign}}</ref> The street fortune teller known as the [[Sariss|Prophetess]] told Wuher that he was the reincarnation of [[Cedo Partu]], the original builder of the cantina. After hearing of this, Wuher banned the Prophetess from entering the cantina.<ref name="SWI91">{{InsiderCite|91|Refresher Reading}}</ref>

Wuher knew [[Mirax Terrik Horn|Mirax Terrik]] well and developed a little "game" with her whereby he would point out to troublemakers that she was the daughter of [[Booster Terrik]]. They played this trick during [[Bacta War|the Bacta War]], on an occasion when [[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]] and Mirax visited the cantina on their way to [[Huff Darklighter]]'s estate.

==Behind the scenes==
In the audio dramatization of ''[[Nightlily: The Lovers' Tale]]'', Wuher was voiced by [[Steve Winfield]].

Wuher was only known as "The Bartender" at the time of the film's release. The [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] source the ''[[Mos Eisley Cantina Adventure Set]]'' gave the character's name as "Cedo Partu" in [[1989]]. In [[1995]], "[[Be Still My Heart: The Bartender's Tale]]" from the ''[[Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina]]'' anthology named him "Wuher", which has been his official name ever since.<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|wuher|Wuher}}</ref> [[Pablo Hidalgo]] created a [[Retroactive continuity|retcon]] in [[Star Wars Insider 91|''Star Wars Insider'' 91]] to acknowledge the latter name [[Cedo Partu]] as a separate character, and the Prophetess's claim that Wuher was the reincarnated soul of Cedo Partu.<ref name="Impact">{{SW|url=news/the-big-impact-of-west-end-games-star-wars-miniatures|text=The Big Impact of West End Games' ''Star Wars'' Miniatures|nolive=1}}</ref>

In the Nintendo DS version of ''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]'', Wuher can fly across gaps like an [[Astromech droid/Legends|Astromech droid]].
